topics.topic: Definition and permissions of owner and staff actors
questions: Are the owner and staff distinct actors, who may become staff, and does possession of the shared staff credential alone make a caller staff?
Are owner and staff distinct principals, who qualifies as staff, and may staff use the API directly or only through owner-configured tools such as the frontend server and operator?

quotes:
Each writing service holds a service token that names it; staff hold a staff
credential. Every write needs one of them; recording, correcting, reading or
erasing a customer needs the staff credential.
How the frontend obtains the staff credential belongs to the frontend.

how a credential's holder is checked against the 'who'
of each action, and what each service token may do;
judgement.why: The authentication rule that determines whether possession of a credential qualifies its holder for an action is explicitly carried to State 2.

topics.topic: Whether operator host access permits reading Registry secrets and service tokens
questions: Does the operator's use of the owner's host access permit it to read Registry configuration and thereby obtain service tokens, or is its filesystem access technically restricted away from secrets?
Can an operator agent using the owner's host access read Registry configuration and therefore obtain service tokens, or is its host access technically restricted to the store and staff credential?

quotes:
It acts for the
owner and holds the staff credential for every action it takes, publishing
and reading a customer's phone included; it holds no service token.

An
agent works with the owner's own access to Registry's host and could read
the store itself, so the credential does not keep contact data from it:

An instance's configuration is set on its host, readable only by the owner and
the Registry process: on the VPS the compose environment file, on a local
instance the environment it is started with.

The owner generates each service
token and the staff credential, keeps the original in the owner's own password
vault (Bitwarden), and writes it into Registry's configuration and into the
configuration of its holders: a service token into the one service it names,
the one staff credential into each tool acting as staff — the operator, a
frontend server.
judgement.divergence: One implementation gives the operator agent unrestricted use of the owner's host access, allowing it to read Registry configuration and obtain service tokens; another restricts that access so it can read the store and its staff credential but not service tokens. The owner, the operator agent, and services accepting those tokens notice the difference.
judgement.why: The operator's trust boundary is unresolved because the text simultaneously denies it service tokens and gives it the owner's host access without stating whether that access reaches the configuration containing those tokens.

topics.topic: Whether staff-only contact data may be disclosed to external model providers
questions: Does “readable by staff only” describe only Registry API authorization, allowing an external model provider to receive the data, or is disclosure to any non-staff party prohibited?

Does “readable by staff only” describe only Registry API authorization, with model providers explicitly permitted to receive the data as external processors, or must contact data remain undisclosed to every non-staff party?

quotes:
Name, phone, e-mail and language are
all the customer's contact data: personal data, readable by staff only (R0-09),
and erasable as a whole.

every contact field it records or reads passes to the provider of the
model the owner runs it on — today Anthropic for Claude Code, OpenAI for
Codex — under that provider's own terms. Registry does not limit which
fields or which provider, and the owner accepts this (owner, 2026-10-27).
judgement.why: The text explicitly permits an operator acting as staff to pass contact data to the owner's model provider, so staff-only describes Registry access rather than an absolute ban on downstream disclosure.

topics.topic: Scope and transmitting component of model-provider disclosure during onboarding
questions: Does the model-provider disclosure apply only to an AI agent, or also to every execution of the `onboard_object` script; and which component actually transmits the contact fields to the provider?

topics.topic: Whether the browser may hold the shared staff credential
questions: For the direct same-host browser flow, is the browser itself allowed to receive and hold the staff credential, or must staff actions always pass through a credential-holding server?
